data.title: Breaking News: The biggest breakthrough in the Claude Riemann Hypothesis has been verified by human mathematicians.
data.description:
Author: New Zhiyuan

Claude's proof on the Riemann Hypothesis has been thoroughly verified by human mathematicians.

This time, mathematician Youness Lamzouri announced a record for Claude's proof—previously, the mainstream limit was around 41.6%, and mathematicians had only improved it by 0.8% over the past 37 years.

But the mathematicians at Anthropic, using their internal Claude proof, directly improved it by 25.6%!

While not a complete proof of the Riemann Hypothesis, this achievement was enough to cause a seismic shift in the mathematical community, with Anthropic dominating headlines. However, AI's proof was obscure and difficult to understand; "the main mechanism is not immediately apparent." Now, number theorist Youness Lamzouri has written a proof that is remarkably concise, ingenious, and elegant—a truly remarkable feat. And in just a few hours, AxiomProver formalized this work. This era is truly exciting! This is not only a display of AI's violent aesthetics, but also a desperate counterattack by human wisdom, culminating in a "cross-species" collaborative myth finalized by another AI (AxiomProver). The underlying logic of the history of mathematics was completely rewritten on this day. (Lean certificate: https://github.com/AxiomMath/ZetaZeros) AI's "Brute Force Aesthetics" Unlocks the Door to the Riemann Hypothesis. The Riemann Hypothesis is revered as the "Holy Grail of Mathematics." Why? Because it, with its purest abstraction, resonates with the most profound reality of the universe. First, it is the ultimate blueprint for taming "prime numbers." Prime numbers, seemingly random and ghostly distributed on the number line, are ingeniously connected to the zeros of the Zeta function by Riemann. If this conjecture holds true, it proves that beneath this chaotic appearance lies a perfectly harmonious symphony. Secondly, it is the "load-bearing wall" of modern mathematics. Today, thousands of higher-order theorems rely on the premise that the Riemann Hypothesis is true. If it were disproven, half of the edifice of analytic number theory would instantly become worthless. From number theory, algebra, and geometry to functional analysis, there are approximately 30 to 50 truly groundbreaking equivalent forms of the Riemann Hypothesis, and the search for these equivalent forms is itself a major focus of modern mathematical research. Oxford University Press has published a three-volume book, *The Equivalent Form of the Riemann Hypothesis*. Surprisingly, it transcends disciplinary boundaries. Physicists were astonished to discover that the spacing of these purely mathematical zeros miraculously matches the energy level distribution of heavy atomic nuclei in quantum mechanics! Proving it is not only a victory for mathematics, but also humanity's ultimate leap into the deepest code of the universe. As is well known, the core of the Riemann Hypothesis is to explore where the non-trivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function lie. In 1859, Riemann boldly conjectured that all non-trivial zeros are neatly arranged on a "critical line" with a real part of 1/2. Proving that 100% of the zeros lie on the critical line would solve the Riemann Hypothesis. Humanity had previously painstakingly proven that more than two-fifths of the zeros lie on this line, and then seemed to have hit a roadblock. Until AI entered the fray. In his latest research, Claude launched a full-scale attack on this century-old problem. AI doesn't understand "a flash of inspiration"; it believes in "brute force." Claude painstakingly calculated the trace and Hilbert-Schmidt norm of a matrix using a set of enormous matrices that grow with N(T), and finally, through a complex set of rank-trace inequalities, he secured the lower bound of the zeros, pushing the boundary to 67.25%! The result was also preliminarily verified by mathematicians Alpöge and Furman. The result caused a global uproar. Humanity was only 32.75% away from completely defeating the Riemann Hypothesis! But when human mathematicians received the AI's proof, they all fell silent. This proof is too ugly. Or rather, it's too "inhuman." Through exhaustive search and splicing, Claude forcibly combined two mathematical tools that seem completely unrelated to human intuition. It's filled with a massive amount of complex tools and obscure matrix transformations. It's like a rampaging bulldozer, carving a bloody path through a roadless rainforest. Can this path be followed? Yes. Is this path easy? Even top mathematicians find it perplexing. As Fields Medal winner Terence Tao, hailed as "the smartest mind of our time," once aptly pointed out: The proofs of this type of AI are extremely obscure and difficult to understand; humans need to spend a great deal of time "digesting" them. AI provided humans with answers, but not with "understanding." Is the future of mathematics simply a ruthless computing machine outputting a bunch of truths incomprehensible to humans? Human mathematicians will never admit defeat.

Humanity's Counterattack: A Dimensional Reduction Strike of "Taste" and "Elegance"

Just as the academic community was painfully "digesting" Claude's brute-force proof, mathematicianYouness Lamzouristood up.

Intuition told him:This is wrong, truth shouldn't be presented in this bloated way. Since AI has proven this direction is correct, there must be a more beautiful shortcut!

Next, Youness demonstrated what true "human intelligence" is.

He wielded Occam's razor, decisively cutting away the redundant, complex, and time-growing massive matrices in Claude's proof. He directly reduced the problem using an extremely concise and elegant Hilbert space inequality! The complex lower bound problem was ingeniously transformed into an estimation of the correlation sum, and then the unconditional version of Montgomery's theorem (BGST) was directly applied. With a few swift strokes, it was effortless and effortless. Both Claude and Youness prove that ">67% of the zeros lie on the critical line." If Claude's proof is a steam engine monster of violent aesthetics, then Youness's proof is a perfectly crafted, flawless sword. The Axiom team generously praised it on social media: Lamzouri reproved the same result, replacing a large number of complex tools with an elegant Hilbert space inequality. A concise and clear proof, showcasing taste and human wisdom. Please note this word: ...

Machines complete the game in hours! The mathematics world is completely transformed

If you think the story ends here with the cliché of "humans defeating AI," you're sorely mistaken.

The climax is just beginning.

Following the traditional rules of the mathematics community, Youness has written this extremely elegant paper. What should be done next?

According to the conventions of the traditional mathematics community, Youness has written this extremely elegant paper. What should be done next?

Find a few top peers, hold a seminar, and spend months or even years reviewing and verifying it line by line. After all, this is the Riemann Hypothesis! Back then, Shinichi Mochizuki proved the ABC conjecture, but because the proof was so complex, the mathematical community debated it for almost ten years without reaching a complete consensus. But this time, times have changed. Within just a few hours of Youness sharing the preprint draft—and I emphasize, just a few hours!—the AI ​​tool AxiomProver automatically and directly formalized Youness's proof using the Lean formal verification language, achieving seamless machine-level verification! This means that while the general public is still figuring out what Hilbert space is, the machine has already ruthlessly dissected the entire logical chain of the proof from beginning to end, delivering a definitive answer. This represents a major breakthrough in human history regarding the Riemann Hypothesis, an epic problem, achieved through machine verification on the very first day of the paper's publication! The Axiom team couldn't hide their excitement: We firmly believe that formal verification using machines, in tandem with new breakthroughs in cutting-edge mathematics, will be an inevitable future. Less than 24 hours later, the Axiom team announced a significant step forward in the twin prime conjecture: There are infinitely many pairs of primes whose intervals do not exceed 2^12. The twin prime conjecture states that there are infinitely many pairs of prime numbers that differ by 2. For centuries, the existence of infinitely many pairs of prime numbers with a finite difference was unknown. In 2014, Yitang Zhang, James Maynard, Terence Tao, and the Polymath project achieved a historic breakthrough, reducing this difference to 246. James Maynard received the Fields Medal for his contributions. By August 31st of this year, mathematician Julia Stadlmann had reduced this difference to 240. On September 3rd, number theorists, applied mathematicians, and engineers, along with AxiomProver, building on the work of Julia Stadlmann, achieved a result of 2^12 through extensive experiments on a large distributed cluster. They stated that the distance between human dreams and proofs can be just hours, not lifetimes. Currently, the draft has been published, and the final version and the Lean formal proof commitment have been released on arXiv. Paper: https://primegaps.axiommath.ai/bgp212.pdf A few hours later, OpenAI used its latest model, Astra, with a new method to reduce this number to 186. Even more shocking is that Fermat's Last Theorem was also thoroughly formalized by Claude. This is the most chilling part of this major event: The inefficient classical era of traditional mathematics—"proposing a conjecture—proving—a lengthy manual peer review—confirmation"—has officially come to an end today. Epilogue: The final 32.75%, who will break the deadlock? Today, we can pop the champagne and celebrate! Over 67% of the zeta zero point is firmly pinned to that magical critical line. The line that Riemann casually drew 167 years ago is being illuminated inch by inch by humans and machines working together. But don't forget, this journey spanning a century is not over. The Riemann Hypothesis still has that final, mysterious 32.75%, like dark matter.

data.title: Base: X account attacked; Robinhood Chain has the highest transaction volume across the entire network.
data.description:
Headline

▌Base Co-founder: X Account Attacked and Fraudulent Token Issued, Users Warned for Security

On September 6th, Base co-founder Jesse Pollak stated that his X account had been attacked. The attackers used a third-party application connected to his X account to issue a fraudulent token. The related posts have since been deleted, all third-party application connections have been removed, and the account has been fully regained. Users are reminded to be vigilant for security. Community feedback indicates that the attackers issued a token called BASE MEME, which has plummeted by over 90% since Jesse Pollak's clarification.

... On September 6th, according to DeFiLlama data, Robinhood Chain's 24-hour DEX trading volume briefly reached $1.89 billion, surpassing Solana Chain's $1.882 billion and ranking first across the entire network. As of press time, according to CoinGecko data: BTC price is $80,010.7, a 24-hour change of +0.25%; ETH price is $2,489.37, a 24-hour change of +1.53%; BNB price is $770.19, a 24-hour change of +7.21%. [Link to coinreaders.com](https://www.coinreaders.com/256739); SOL price is $103.39, up 1.65% in 24 hours; DOGE price is $0.094, up 12% in 24 hours. href="https://www.tgju.org/news/3876630/%d8%af%d9%88%d8%ac-%da%a9%d9%88%db %8c%d9%86-doge-%d9%86%d8%a7%da%af%d9%87%d8%a7%d9%86-%d8%a8%d8%a7-%d8%b1%d8% b4%d8%af-%d8%af%d9%88-%d8%b1%d9%82%d9%85%db%8c-%d8%a7%d9%81%d8%b2%d8%a7%db% 8c%d8%b4-%d9%85%db%8c-%db%8c%d8%a7%d8%a8%d8%af-%d8%af%d8%b1-%d8%ad%d8%a7%d9 %84%db%8c-%da%a9%d9%87-%d8%aa%d8%ad%d9%84%db%8c%d9%84%da%af%d8%b1%d8%a7%d9% 86-%d8%a2%d8%ba%d8%a7%d8%b2-%d9%81%d8%b5%d9%84-%d8%a2%d9%84%d8%aa-%da%a9%d9 XRP price is $1.4169, 24-hour change

Policy

▌Japan to Strengthen Review of Banks' Lending to Overseas Non-Bank Lenders

On September 6, according to the Nikkei, Japan's Financial Services Agency (FSA) will review whether Japanese financial institutions have adequately assessed the credit risks associated with lending to overseas non-bank lenders and real estate companies. This idea will be incorporated into the agency's draft annual strategic priorities plan, which is being finalized by June next year. Major Japanese banks are expanding their overseas non-bank lending operations, and so-called non-bank financial intermediaries are expanding globally and increasingly obtaining financing from Japanese banks. In the real estate sector, soaring housing prices in major metropolitan areas have prompted regional banks and other financial institutions to increase related lending. The FSA believes it is necessary to further examine these credit risks. In addition, the FSA will also focus on reviewing investment and loan policies, project reviews, and risk management for facilities such as data centers.

(Jinshi) Trump's MAGA Super PAC Donates $10 Million to Election Campaign for the First Time According to Politico, a document released Saturday shows that President Trump's "Make America Great Again" super PAC (MAGA Inc.) will donate $10 million to Ken Paxton's Senate campaign. This is the committee's first election contribution before the November midterm elections. Republicans have been urging Trump to use his vast campaign funds, complaining that Trump must personally help Paxton win in Texas. Trump stated, "We're going to put in a lot of money because we don't want to lose our country. I'll put in all the necessary funds to help us, and that money comes from MAGA, money I control." At a press conference in the Oval Office on Friday, Trump pledged to spend "potentially $400 million to $500 million" in the midterm elections, and said the super PAC had already raised "close to $1 billion." (Jinshi) Caixin: Hong Kong SFC raids Huatai Financial Holdings' offices, suspected of insider trading. On September 6, according to Caixin, the Hong Kong Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) raided the offices of Huatai Financial Holdings (Hong Kong) in August and questioned employees about a suspected insider trading case involving US stock options. Multiple sources familiar with the matter said the investigation may be related to an options trading incident in May: some investors are accused of trading related options before Chinese regulators tightened regulations on Futu Holdings and Tiger Brokers' cross-border brokerage business, profiting more than US$100 million. Caixin previously reported that the US has filed a lawsuit in the case and disclosed that more than 310 accounts are involved. Cryptocurrency ▌The 90-day correlation between Bitcoin and gold prices has risen to +0.50, reaching a high since the 2020 pandemic. According to The Kobeissi Letter on September 6th, the price movements of Bitcoin and gold are becoming increasingly synchronized: the 90-day correlation between Bitcoin and gold prices has risen to +0.50, approaching the historical high reached during the 2020 pandemic. This figure has more than doubled since the beginning of this year. In contrast, after the recovery from the 2022 bear market, the 90-day correlation between Bitcoin and gold peaked at +0.30. The recent rapid increase in correlation was mainly accelerated after the US Treasury announced on August 19th that it would at least double the size of its long-term Treasury bond repurchase operations. The US Treasury plans to increase the size of each repurchase operation from $2 billion to $4 billion. Meanwhile, the 90-day correlation between Bitcoin and the Nasdaq 100 index has fallen to approximately +0.30, a near one-year low. Investors are increasingly viewing gold and Bitcoin as assets to hedge against currency devaluation. UNI breaks through $6.50. Market data shows that UNI has broken through $6.50 and is currently trading at $6.52, with a 24-hour increase of 3.82%. Price volatility is high; please manage your risk accordingly.

▌Data: USDC deposits into DeFi protocols grew by 34.1% in the past 90 days, reaching $9.3 billion

On September 6th, according to Token Terminal monitoring, in the past 90 days, the amount of USDC issued by Circle deposited into DeFi protocols grew by 34.1%, reaching $9.3 billion. Among them, Morpho Blue and Aave V3 had USDC deposits of $3.6 billion and $2.8 billion respectively, accounting for approximately 69% of the total.

Jake Chervinsky: If Meme returns to the mainstream, it is expected to become a key issue in crypto policy. On September 6th, Hyperliquid Policy Center CEO Jake Chervinsky stated that policymakers did not prioritize Meme regulation in the previous cycle because most believed it was just a short-lived trend, a view reinforced by the subsequent sharp decline in trading volume. If Meme experiences significant renewed growth and enters the mainstream market, it is expected to become a major regulatory issue in crypto policy.

▌Arthur Hayes Buys 244,000 UNI Tokens, Worth Approximately $1.73 Million

On September 6th, according to Ember Monitoring, an hour earlier, BitMEX co-founder Arthur Hayes bought 244,000 UNI tokens through Flowdesk OTC trading, worth approximately $1.73 million, at a purchase price of $7.06.

▌Huang Licheng: Withdraws Acquisition Offer for Friend.tech, Supports Platform Relaunch on Robinhood Chain

On September 5th, Huang Licheng posted on the X platform that he speculated his acquisition offer for Friend.tech was blocked by Paradigm, and therefore withdrew the proposal.

He also stated that he would provide support if Racer (co-founder of Friend.tech) relaunches Friend.tech on the Robinhood Chain.

Blockchain and AI Applications

▌TradeXYZ Completes HIP-4 DEX Deployment

On September 6th, on-chain data showed that TradeXYZ had completed the deployment of its HIP-4 DEX. TradeXYZ was previously one of the main deployers in the Hyperliquid HIP-3 market, and this deployment signifies its further expansion from perpetual contracts to the HIP-4 prediction market. Previous on-chain data showed that it had prepared an additional 500,000 HYPE tokens for HIP-4 deployment.

Blockchain and AI Applications

▌TradeXYZ Completes HIP-4 DEX Deployment

Important Economic Developments ▌Putin: Russia Has Not Yet Discussed Expanding the Ceasefire with Ukraine On September 6, according to RIA Novosti, Russian President Vladimir Putin stated that Kyiv has called for an expansion of the ceasefire, but Russia has not yet consulted with Ukraine on this matter. "The Ukrainian authorities have called for a broader three-day ceasefire, but we have never reached an agreement with them on this," Putin said during a meeting with US Special Envoy Witkov and Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner. (Jinshi) Iranian Lawmaker: The US Should Not Have Engaged in Blockade Actions On September 6, according to Al Jazeera, a senior Iranian lawmaker confirmed that Iran had used ballistic missiles to attack US warships. Hassan Ghashgavi, a spokesman for the Iranian parliament's National Security Committee, stated, "Yes, we fully confirm this. We are engaged in a life-or-death struggle with the United States. Their military action naturally violates all international law." He added, "Because the United States is far away from us, it doesn't consider this war a matter of life or death." When asked about Iran changing the rules of engagement, Ghashgavi stated that "this blockade should never have existed in the first place," pointing to the now-expired memorandum of understanding. "Four days ago, the Iranian president stated at the Bishkek summit that we are ready to return to the negotiating table, but US officials ignored this and instead continued to escalate and strengthen the blockade." (Jin Shi)

▌Kremlin aide Ushakov: Putin is ready to cooperate with the US to seek a diplomatic solution to the Russia-Ukraine issue

On September 6, Kremlin aide Ushakov stated that Putin is ready to cooperate with the US to seek a diplomatic solution to the Russia-Ukraine issue. The talks between Putin and the US envoy were "extremely frank" and the atmosphere was one of mutual trust. Putin's talks with Witkov and Kushner lasted 3 hours and 10 minutes.

(Jinshi) On the 5th local time, the military conflict between the US and Iran continued, with the US claiming to have struck three Iranian oil tankers that day. Subsequently, Iran stated that "the US military, out of desperation due to the blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, attacked three Iranian oil tankers and caused damage." In response, Iran attacked multiple oil tankers and US vessels, while warning ships in the Persian Gulf to avoid navigating illegal waterways. Analysts point out that with the ongoing military actions of both sides and the lack of a solution to the Strait of Hormuz issue, the regional situation will remain volatile in the short term. (CCTV News) Can Bitcoin still be called "digital gold" under the geopolitical crisis? Every geopolitical crisis causes gold prices to rise while Bitcoin prices plummet. After six tests, the claim of "digital gold" has never been substantiated by data. Countries hoard gold but exclude Bitcoin from their reserves. For investors, Bitcoin exhibits asymmetry: it falls with stocks but doesn't rise with them. Three structural asymmetries prevent Bitcoin from achieving safe-haven status: an overabundance of derivatives (market structure), the dominance of leveraged traders (participant composition), and a lack of repeatable behavioral records (behavioral accumulation). Bitcoin is not a safe-haven asset, but it is a "crisis-useful asset," capable of functioning when borders are closed and banks fail. If these three asymmetries narrow, Bitcoin may no longer be a replica of gold but a completely new "next-generation gold." Generational shifts and the widespread adoption of algorithms are key factors that could accelerate this process.

data.title: Robinhood Chain Erupts: "Tokenization of US Stocks" Collide with Speculative Frenzy
data.description:
Source: *The Chopping Block*; Compiled by: Felix, PANews

Recently, Unchained founder Laura Shin, along with Dragonfly managing partner Haseeb Qureshi, general partner Tom Schmidt, and Robot Ventures managing partner Tarun Chitra, analyzed the "US stock tokenization + Meme coin" frenzy on Robinhood Chain, the competitive landscape of Solana, and Hyperliquid's compliance battles in its attempt to enter the US compliant market on the podcast *The Chopping Block*.

During the discussion, the guests held differing opinions on the cultural phenomenon of retail investors seeking "entertainment value" in high-risk trading. Some believed it was pure capitalist destruction, while others viewed it as an emerging token distribution model. They also mentioned rumors that Hyperliquid was attempting to enter the US compliant market through a partnership with Kraken's Payword.

PANews has compiled the highlights of the discussion. Haseeb: The hottest narrative this week is undoubtedly the rise of Robinhood Chain. When Robinhood Chain initially launched, trading volume surged and then declined, leading many to believe it might be a flash in the pan. But now, Robinhood Chain is experiencing a second wave of explosive growth, with over 125,000 active wallets, 5.7 million daily transactions, DEX daily trading volume exceeding $1.2 billion, and daily blockchain transaction fee revenue reaching $2 million. This surge is largely driven by on-chain tokenized stocks and Meme Coin. This also fueled the surge in Arbitrum's price, as the Robinhood Chain is built on the Arbitrum Stack, and a significant portion of the transaction fees generated by the Robinhood Chain are returned to Arbitrum and Robinhood. Ethereum also received a small share of the data availability (DA) fees, but very little. This has led to much debate: Does this prove that L1 cannot capture value from the L2 boom above it? Is this a negative for L1? Tom: I'm very surprised. This is a "company chain," yet it generates such amazing on-chain activity. What's even more interesting is that about half of the trading volume comes from tokenized stocks, not just Meme coins. I'm curious about the Robinhood team's reaction now. I dare say that when they initially planned this chain, their beautiful vision was: "We're going to build a completely new financial system, 24/7 stock trading, a global, permissionless, open mainnet..." And now? Everyone's frantically trading all sorts of vulgar Meme coins. But there's definitely a very real human element to it. Tarun, as a "Robinhood Chain spokesperson," what's your take on this?

Tarun: I wouldn't dare call myself a Robinhood Chain spokesperson. But I must say, seeing the "M forks" (Ohm forks) resurface in 2026 is exhilarating.

For those unfamiliar, let me explain: Ohm (OlympusDAO) was a very famous, somewhat Ponzi-like stablecoin experiment on Ethereum in 2022. It spawned the (3,3) meme and ultimately collapsed in 2022. Although its original protocol survived, it's far from what it used to be.

And now, these people on Robinhood Chain have cleverly applied the "Ohm fork mechanism" to Meme coins.

In short, these Ohm forks are now utilizing Meme Coin in a highly creative way. These contracts aren't simply copied; they've been modified enough that you can think of them as a kind of "Meme Coin launch platform." When you issue a Meme Coin, you must bind it to an underlying tokenized stock. The logic is: to mint a Meme Coin, you essentially have to buy that tokenized stock and lock a portion of it in a liquidity pool. For example, if you use $100 worth of stock to mint, you'll receive $10 worth of Meme Coins, locked in the LP pool, and the remaining $90 will be returned to you. The locked $10 is used to provide liquidity, much like a classic bonding curve mechanism. But what's truly interesting is that this stock pairing effectively turns Meme Coin into a "token incentive" for a particular stock. Recall the Ohm example. There was Ohm, locked Ohm, and ETH. ETH was like the stock; everything revolved around it. Locked Ohm was used to provide liquidity to ensure you could redeem ETH, while Ohm itself was the incentive. The most classic example is the wildly popular Meme coin "BONER." The BONER token was paired with HIMS' tokenized stock. HIMS is an online men's health drug retailer that advertises extensively in New York City. The BONER coin essentially became the "liquidity incentive" for minting HIMS stock tokens. Haseeb: Everyone was frantically trading BONER coin over the weekend when the US stock market was closed. Because of the Meme coin's surge, the price of the HIMS stock token paired with it on the DEX also de-pegged significantly, far exceeding the US stock market's closing price last Friday. Many retail investors, fueled by FOMO (Fear of Missing Out), frantically bought Meme coin on Robinhood Chain or FOMO aggregators, believing its price would continue to rise. However, when the US stock market opened on Monday morning, arbitrage opportunities opened, allowing anyone to mint new HIMS shares and bring them onto the chain. These retail investors who bought BONER and premium HIMS at high prices on Sunday night were ruthlessly wiped out by hedge funds and arbitrageurs on Monday morning, their accounts instantly wiped out. Retail investors cheered for Meme coin's rise, but in reality, every time they pushed Meme coin up over the weekend, they were handing over real money to Wall Street hedge funds through this massive "de-anchoring." This group is even celebrating this behavior—it's insane. Tarun: I think this is somewhat similar to DeFi Summer meeting GameStop retail frenzy, while also being mixed with 4chan culture (a unique internet subculture originating from the well-known anonymous image forum 4chan, characterized by its deconstructive, anonymized, anti-establishment, and meme-filled nature) and tokenized stocks. In a way, this is "investment idiocy." Tom: There is indeed a peculiar "generational culture" and entertainment value here: "Haha, let's see how much money we can lose!" Haseeb: But this is really stupid. GameStop at least had a theory that we should defeat Wall Street and save companies through a joint short squeeze. But the mathematical logic here is completely flawed. The amount of capital in these on-chain tokenized stocks is negligible compared to the underlying real stocks in the US stock market; you can't possibly short anyone. If you ask your AI, "Hey, I want to short Wall Street by buying a Meme coin, do you think it's feasible?" your AI will definitely answer, "Are you out of your mind? Hand over your private key, you're banned from trading." This is purely the Meme coin game. Every cycle has a new game, this time it's just wrapped in RWA. Laura: I agree with Haseeb's point of view, this is really bad. Although my initial comments were just observations, if we're making a value judgment, I side with Haseeb. Because after this bear market, retail investors have basically been completely wiped out. They suffered from various crashes and the ruthless exploitation of the Meme coin ecosystem. Many ordinary people have completely withdrawn from cryptocurrency. A few days ago I invited Jeff Dorman on my show, and we talked about how, from all objective indicators, the underlying infrastructure of the crypto industry (such as stablecoin adoption, compliance progress, ETFs, etc.) is at its best level in history. But I told him, "Because the last Memecoin frenzy hurt retail investors so badly, even with the best objective facts, market sentiment remains extremely low." He couldn't understand this perspective at the time. Those retail investors who lost everything in the trenches didn't care about "stablecoins being adopted by the mainstream" or "ETFs being approved"; they only knew they had lost everything. Therefore, we, as industry voices, should absolutely not encourage or whitewash this mechanism that is "designed to make retail investors lose money to hedge funds." Tarun: I understand your moral condemnation. But from an anthropological perspective, it's indeed very interesting. RWA has always been considered the most boring, least incentivized, and most difficult to promote area in the crypto industry. This mechanism successfully injected a token incentive into RWA, and within a week, it boosted the issuance of RWA on the Robinhood Chain by 50%, reaching $70-80 million. This demonstrates that sufficient demand will force new issuance. While retail investors may have been drawn by the BONER coin, the ultimately tokenized HIMS stock remained on the chain. Haseeb: But the difference between a casino and this is that people who play slot machines at a casino know they are spending and having fun; they know that mathematically they are losing money. But the retail investors rushing into these Meme coins are deceived by KOLs and promotional rhetoric on various social media platforms. They firmly believe they are making money and can achieve financial freedom. This "illusion of making money" is the most deadly and cruel thing. Haseeb: The next important question is, is Robinhood Chain stealing Solana's thunder now? Trader Flood tweeted, "Solana is in its most dangerous position since its inception." Some arguments are that Solana was the first to tokenize stocks and previously had a near-monopoly on Memecoin. So, if people want to mix RWA and Memecoin, why is this happening on Robinhood Chain instead of Solana? Furthermore, Solana currently lacks any perpetual contract exchange with substantial market share and has virtually no RWA market share (currently dominated by Robinhood and Ethereum). Many mainstream trading pairs on Solana are now increasingly being paired with stablecoins like USDC instead of SOL. This seems to indicate that while Solana had a first-mover advantage, it is now being forcefully usurped by Robinhood, a latecomer. Many people are fiercely debating on X, arguing whether retail investors underestimated Solana, or whether Solana simply entered the market too early, becoming a stepping stone for Robinhood to explore new avenues. Or, as Tarun said, if most users enter through FOMO, then the underlying chain is irrelevant to retail investors because the binding and locking effects of the underlying chain have disappeared. What do you all think? Will this be Solana's death knell? Laura: This reminds me of a very interesting anecdote: I heard that Robinhood Chain almost chose to build on Solana, but at the last minute, they changed their minds and went with Arbitrum. At the time, the Arbitrum Foundation and the Solana Foundation interacted frequently on Twitter, clearly indicating a fierce competition between them, which was later reported by some media outlets. I interviewed AJ on the show at the time. While he didn't directly confirm whether Robinhood was extremely close to choosing Solana, he explained, "When you have your own dedicated L2, the entire economic model changes completely—you're no longer simply paying money to the underlying chain; you can even divert and earn money (fee sharing)." Therefore, if Robinhood had indeed chosen to build on Solana, perhaps Solana would be in a completely different, much better position now. Tarun: There's a long-standing rule in the crypto industry: those who start early often end up late. Those who first propose a concept but fail to execute it well often watch as others reap the rewards. For example, the earliest DEXs weren't the ones with the largest trading volume, and the earliest prediction markets weren't the current Polymarkets. Solana made a serious strategic mistake in its previous efforts to integrate with US stock tokenization. Solana's initial collaboration with XStocks (a tokenized stock provider) went awry. The Solana Foundation had significantly incentivized XStocks' liquidity on Solana, but subsequently allowed XStocks to be acquired by Kraken. This is a delicate matter: either you invest directly and form a deep alliance, or you design an extremely aligned incentive mechanism. Simply throwing money into an ecosystem will ultimately result in a lack of loyalty to the chain itself. Haseeb: I think it's too early to write Solana's epitaph. Because if you look at the trading data, Solana remains the absolute leader in 30-day DEX trading volume, and with a huge advantage. Over the past 30 days, Solana's DEX trading volume reached $62 billion, while the entire Robinhood Chain only reached $17 billion, Ethereum $33 billion, followed by BSC, Base, and then Robinhood Chain. Tom: Even looking at FOMO trading volume alone, Solana and Robinhood Chain were neck and neck a week ago. Haseeb: Yes. Based on today's 24-hour trading volume, Solana still holds the top spot with $2.5 billion; Robinhood Chain is second with $1.5 billion; and Ethereum is third with $1.3 billion. So Robinhood Chain has indeed surged to second place today. Laura, what are your thoughts on Solana vs Robinhood? Laura: I mentioned FOMO earlier because it's a major trend. At the wallet and application level, users are breaking free from the lock-in of specific blockchain ecosystems. People are now very accustomed to various cross-chain bridges that run automatically in the background, especially for small transactions. Although Robinhood has a large traditional retail distribution channel, if you analyze the activity on the Robinhood Chain carefully, you'll find that the vast majority of traffic doesn't come from the official Robinhood app itself, but from third-party aggregator apps. This suggests that these traffic aggregators (such as FOMO and GMGN) may become more significant winners in the future. So it's difficult to determine who wins and who loses now. Haseeb: Exactly. Currently, about half of the transaction volume comes from FOMO, and the other half from GMGN. In terms of user numbers, the vast majority of users are on FOMO (Fear of Influence), meaning that GMGN users are mainly "professional traders" or bots, whose individual trades are much larger. They are more like the "sharks" in a pond than the "shrimp" destined to lose money on FOMO. Furthermore, although Robinhood Chain's daily trading volume has surged to second place, its TVL (TVL) remains extremely small. Robinhood Chain's TVL is currently only $730 million, ranking only 11th among public chains. In comparison, Solana's TVL reaches $5.7 billion, Base has $5.4 billion, and Ethereum dominates with $48 billion. Therefore, it's too early to draw conclusions. And I still maintain my previous view: I haven't seen a large influx of new retail investors from across the crypto space. This remains an internal frenzy within the crypto industry. Haseeb: Previously, it was reported that the U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) was seeking to bring Hyperliquid under the U.S. regulatory framework. According to a recent Bloomberg report, Hyperliquid Labs is currently in deep talks with Kraken's parent company, Payword. The two companies may establish a joint venture, allowing Hyperliquid to leverage Kraken's Bitnomial license and clearinghouse to launch in the U.S. market while remaining compliant. Of course, this U.S. version of Hyperliquid will require mandatory KYC (Know Your Customer) verification and will involve some form of cross-border liquidity integration with their overseas main liquidity pools; the specific operational mechanism is currently unclear. Interestingly, after the news broke, the stock price of traditional derivatives giant CME (Chicago Mercantile Exchange) fell in the U.S. stock market, while Hyperliquid's token (HYPE) surged. What are your thoughts on Hyperliquid launching in the U.S.? What impact will this have? Tarun: I think this is very similar to what Tom mentioned last week. It's more likely to end up as a stripped-down version of Polymarket (US version) or Robinhood (simplified version), rather than achieving true, unified global liquidity. This is because the regulatory requirements for fund management, risk limits, and automatic liquidation (ADL) and forced liquidation mechanisms in decentralized exchanges are completely different under the US compliance framework. This is certainly beneficial for Hyperliquid's brand expansion, but it will definitely not be exactly the same as the overseas version. But that's enough. Just like Polymarket US, despite being criticized within the industry, still achieved significant growth due to the timing of the World Cup and the US election. Laura: What I'd like to know is, will this compliant version still be a pure "DeFi" exchange (similar to the HIP-3 architecture), or will it become something else? Tarun: The biggest obstacle is the centralized clearing requirements in the US. Under the regulatory framework, you must have a central clearinghouse, which usually doesn't allow the instantaneous ADL (automatic liquidation) or algorithmic liquidation mechanisms found in DeFi. Even if it were possible, it would require bridging a huge legal and technical gap. Therefore, while it may nominally run on-chain (a HIP-3 instance), for professional traders, it requires the full suite of CeFi heavy equipment, such as prime brokers, market surveillance, and anti-manipulation systems, resulting in a completely different experience and feel compared to the overseas version. For large funds and institutions, this is a completely different game. Tom: I completely agree. This is very similar to what we discussed last week. The core question is: can you create a synergistic effect of "1+1>2" between the US compliant version and the overseas version? This reminds me of a perhaps inappropriate analogy: if Binance.US had been extremely successful, could it have benefited BNB? We don't know. Moreover, overseas star brands often encounter difficulties adapting to the US market. Tarun: Look at past attempts by international exchanges to enter the US market—FTX.US, Binance.US, and OKX's US entities—they basically all failed, becoming a "graveyard" for the crypto industry. This is mainly because the cumbersome US regulations completely crippled the product's user experience (UX). You almost have to rebuild an entire compliance and technical architecture from scratch locally; a Kraken license alone cannot help you achieve this overnight. Laura: I completely understand the motivations behind US regulation, but my concern is: as cryptocurrencies become a more mainstream system in the future, if the US completely isolates itself from the global crypto market through extremely stringent compliance walls, won't this create a conflict between an "American-style firewall LAN" and the "global internet"? In the long run, is this proactive isolation from the most dynamic global liquidity truly beneficial to the US? Tarun: Indeed, it's difficult to imagine how these two systems could seamlessly interoperate at the margin and collateral level. This is because of the difference in underlying legal systems: in the US financial market, if a liquidation agent goes bankrupt due to errors, you can sue them; but on pure blockchain, if you're subject to ADL (automatic liquidation) by a smart contract, you have nowhere to appeal. Different countries (such as Europe, Japan, and the US) inherently have vastly different ways of operating their stock exchanges. Therefore, the globally unified standard of "Internet thinking" often fails when it comes to capital controls and anti-money laundering demands of sovereign states. Tom: Yes, the US has the longest reach of regulation and possesses the world's largest and most fertile single consumer and financial market. This is why global project teams are willing to go to great lengths to comply with US regulations. Laura: In the past, most countries had both "formal markets" and "informal markets (i.e., black/gray markets)." What's unique about the US over the past 50 years is that we've almost eliminated informal stock trading markets; everything operates within a highly compliant formal framework. Cryptocurrencies are essentially bringing this "gray/informal market" to every corner of the globe, including the US. The internet did this at the content level, and cryptocurrencies are replicating this process at the asset level. If you're a highly compliant, regulated institution, you're confined to the US-compliant version of Hyperliquid for trading; but if you're a retail investor operating independently, you'll always find a way to bypass the firewall and connect to the global version, Hyperliquid Global. If one gets blocked, there will be another, and the one after that. This is the borderless, permissionless nature of cryptocurrency. Ultimately, every country may build firewalls similar to those in the US, while decentralized global protocols overseas will, like Napster in its early days, grow wildly in the gray area, unstoppable. Haseeb: I wholeheartedly agree. Unless one day the world's largest companies choose to conduct their initial public offerings (IPOs) directly on-chain, completely bypassing traditional stock exchanges, it's unlikely that existing geopolitical barriers will be completely overturned. But we don't see that trend yet. While cryptocurrencies are borderless at the code level, capital controls and the prevention of capital flight behind liquidity and funds are extremely objective and stringent national priorities. Okay, that's all for today. Thank you for listening, and see you next week!

data.title: Who will win the investment banking race for the "largest IPO in history"?
data.description:
Author: Bu Shuqing, Wall Street Insights

AI unicorn Anthropic is about to launch the largest IPO in Wall Street history, and a battle among top investment banks for underwriting seats is nearing its end.

On Saturday, according to the Financial Times, citing four sources familiar with the matter, Morgan Stanley is in a favorable position to secure the most important "lead left" underwriter position for this IPO, while Goldman Sachs is expected to serve as a stabilizing agent, responsible for overseeing key trading phases in the early stages of Anthropic's listing.

Investors expect Anthropic's listing valuation to reach $2 trillion or more, surpassing SpaceX to become the largest IPO in history. If the valuation comes true, early investors will reap tens of billions of dollars in paper profits. Anthropic's listing performance will also become an important indicator of the current market's risk appetite for high-growth AI companies.

Morgan Stanley leads the pack, Goldman Sachs supports the price, and JPMorgan Chase and others also join. Morgan Stanley holds the most prominent position in the allocation of seats for this IPO. Reports indicate that Morgan Stanley has been leading discussions with potential investors regarding the Anthropic offering price in recent weeks. This is one of the core functions of the lead underwriter – controlling the valuation negotiations and determining which hedge funds, institutional investors, and sovereign wealth funds will receive the largest share of stock allocations. It also represents significant reputational capital for Wall Street investment banks. However, sources also cautioned that Morgan Stanley's final appointment is not yet finalized and remains uncertain. Goldman Sachs is expected to serve as a stabilizing agent. It's worth noting that in SpaceX's IPO in June, the roles of the two banks were reversed—Goldman Sachs served as the lead underwriter, and Morgan Stanley as the stabilizing agent. Each bank received $100 million from a $500 million fee pool shared by over 20 participating institutions. Furthermore, JPMorgan Chase, Citigroup, and Barclays are also expected to secure significant positions in this deal, as these three banks have previously provided debt financing to Anthropic. The IPO may be delayed until mid-October. Anthropic originally planned to submit its IPO prospectus as early as next week, but the timing has not yet been finalized. According to the latest Reuters report, Anthropic has postponed its IPO prospectus submission to late September, with the roadshow starting as early as mid-October, aiming to list before the November midterm elections. This delay is related to the $15 billion credit line the company is finalizing, and further procedures can only proceed after the financing is secured. The IPO will take place shortly after SpaceX completed its record $86 billion financing round in June with a valuation of $1.78 trillion, and the market is closely watching whether it can maintain the high valuation enthusiasm for AI assets. Strong Revenue Growth, But Falling Short of the Most Optimistic Expectations Anthropic's valuation has surged over the past year, currently exceeding $900 billion, and investors expect its IPO valuation to exceed $2 trillion, more than double its current valuation. However, the company's revenue performance has not fully met the most aggressive market expectations. In August, Anthropic informed shareholders that its July revenue, annualized, reached $65 billion, a significant increase from $47 billion in May, but still below the $80 billion annualized sales threshold previously expected by some investors. Meanwhile, competitive pressure cannot be ignored. Anthropic's biggest competitor, OpenAI, has been gaining momentum recently, releasing its latest AI model this week and calling it the "world's smartest" model. Some market analysts warn that OpenAI's strong resurgence may put pressure on Anthropic's IPO valuation. The next battle: OpenAI IPO seats are in sight. This competition for underwriting seats in Anthropic's IPO is merely a prelude to a larger-scale competition. Morgan Stanley and Goldman Sachs will also be vying for the underwriting rights for OpenAI's IPO—which is expected to list early next year. The "lead underwriter" position not only means substantial direct profits but also represents a strategic move for investment banks to build client relationships and market reputation in the AI ​​field. As a wave of AI companies go public, those who can secure leading targets first will gain a competitive advantage in this protracted competition.

data.title: A $150 million emotional speedrun – AMC short squeeze cyclical every 5 years
data.description:
At the close of trading on Thursday, AMC Entertainment closed at $2.54. This largest movie theater chain in the US has a market capitalization of $2.27 billion and 893 million shares outstanding. There was no news on Thursday.

Half an hour after the market closed, a new trading pair appeared on the Robinhood blockchain: AMC/MEME. The new coin's full name is "A Meme Coin," an abbreviation of AMC:MEME.

Then things started to get out of control.


In five hours, the coin MEME surged over a thousandfold, its market capitalization starting at around $3 million, breaking through $30 million, $50 million, and approaching $150 million; at the same time, AMC's own price also fluctuated, with overnight prices rising by over 14%, subsequently expanding to 18% to 20% pre-market. The CEO of AMC and the founder of Robinhood were seen exchanging insults on X late at night. To understand what happened, we need to look back at the history between AMC and Robinhood. Both were bailed out by the same brokerage firm and shut down by the same firm. In 2021, a textbook example of a short squeeze occurred between AMC and Robinhood. On January 28th of that year, Robinhood restricted the purchase of a batch of skyrocketing stocks, allowing only sales. GameStop and AMC were on the list. Retail investors watched the prices plummet on the app, calling the action a betrayal. But retail investors couldn't live without it: Robinhood was the easiest entry point for retail investors at the time, and most of AMC's bullish positions were placed through it. That June, AMC's stock price soared above $72, becoming one of the most discussed stocks in the US. Aron cleverly capitalized on this enthusiasm: he gave free popcorn to shareholders who registered with Investor Connect, befriended bullish investors on social media, and orchestrated rounds of share issuances at high prices, using retail investors' money to pay off debts and stay afloat, pulling the company back from the brink of bankruptcy. At that time, Aron was one of the most beloved CEOs among retail investors. Five years later, the same company and the same CEO turned their attention to a new business at the same brokerage: on-chain tokenized stocks. The name AMC remained the same, the name Robinhood remained the same, but the battlefield of the short squeeze had moved from New York's order book to a 24/7 on-chain pool. What ignited the market this time was the same formula proven in 2021: attention, leverage, and a short squeeze story. Robinhood Chain, a Layer 2 network launching in July 2026, touts "tokenized US stocks": copying New York stocks onto the chain for 24/7 trading, accessible to non-US users. This copied token has its own rules; it moves with the stock price and claims to correspond to custodied underlying shares, but it doesn't grant voting rights or real shares in a New York account. The rules for meme tokens have changed. Previously, creating a meme involved putting ETH or USDT in the pool; now, creators can add NVDA, TSLA, AAPL, or even a movie stock called AMC. The front-end path is cleverly concealed: you see yourself spending stablecoins, but the back-end has already handled it twice for you—first stock tokens, then into a pool to exchange for meme. Even the project team's commission is settled in stock tokens. Thus, the USD price of meme is compressed into a single formula: 1 meme can be exchanged for how many stock tokens, multiplied by the USD price of the stock tokens. Double betting. Betting that meme will outperform a particular stock, while simultaneously gambles your entire fortune on the stock's rise or fall. If the stock rises, the USD price of meme is boosted; if the stock falls, even if meme outperforms, the USD return shrinks. AMC happens to be that asset with its own narrative and memory: in 2021, it was shorted by bears, rescued by retail investors, and shut down by Robinhood. Behind those five letters stands the emotions of an entire generation of retail investors. This kind of strategy has been playing out on the Robinhood chain for a month. For example, BONER, launched on August 20th, directly links its trading pair to the tokenized shadow of Hims & Hers. This company sells men's health products, and BONER's narrative is so straightforward it needs no translation: "hard currency," a short squeeze of HIMS. It coincided with a weekend: the New York market was closed, the issuer could hardly issue more tokens, the pool drained the free circulation, and on-chain HIMS surged from $28.84 at Friday's close to $132.64, more than four times. On Monday's opening, the issuer minted 4,000 new tokens, bringing the shadow back to its original level, but BONER itself continued to rise, driven by sentiment. Next up was FATCOIN, which, after being listed as Lilly's tokenized stock (LLY), used the "the more you speculate, the fatter you get" joke about diet pills to justify its price surge. It jumped 175 times in ten hours. Executives at other companies didn't say anything, but AMC's CEO couldn't sit still. After the CEO's outburst, the price rose even faster. What made the CEO furious was that the on-chain activity had been reflected in his own stock price; a pool he couldn't control was trading using his company's name and price. His first statement was harsh: Robinhood claimed to cover tokenized stocks of over 190 companies, including AMC; this project had nothing to do with AMC, was unauthorized, and not registered under U.S. securities laws. The wording escalated to "disgraceful, absurd, disgusting, and unforgivable," and the board would immediately hire an outside securities lawyer. Tenev replied with "What does this have to do with me?", instantly triggering a second wave of discussion. Aron immediately followed up with a second attack: he claimed that Robinhood was issuing products "representing AMC stock" through an overseas entity in Jersey, yet was not bound by U.S. securities laws, posing a "virtually existential" risk to the company; AMC spends millions of dollars annually on securities compliance, while Robinhood's "synthetic stock market" has separated trading from the financing and ownership of publicly traded companies, giving traditional shareholders voting rights while token holders receive nothing. He demanded that Robinhood voluntarily halt trading of AMC stock tokens, or his lawyers would take action to force a halt and file an inquiry with the SEC. At this point, the issue had spread from the trading pool to Washington. The argument itself became part of the market dynamics. Each round of verbal sparring increased the level of discussion; the higher the discussion, the thicker the buy orders in the pool; the thicker the buy orders, the higher the meme rose; and the higher the meme rose, the more uneasy the CEO became. It was a closed loop, fueled by attention itself. What memes feared most was being ignored. How many zeros away from a short squeeze? Putting aside emotions, what's truly worth calculating is the scale. The total issuance of tokenized AMC is approximately 1.33 million. 1.1 million tokens represent 0.15% of the 893 million shares outstanding. Of these, approximately 746,000 are locked in various pools, with the MEME/AMC main pool alone holding 557,000 tokens, nearly half of the total issuance. Around 700,000 tokens remain in wallets and stablecoin pools for price discovery. Data from the underlying stock is also available: short positions amount to 42.4 million shares, representing 4.78% of the circulating supply; average daily trading volume is approximately 40.25 million shares, equivalent to approximately $100 million to $120 million. Even if all of 0.15% of the share capital were bought, it would only represent a fraction of the average daily trading volume of the underlying stock. For a true short squeeze to occur, a sufficiently large buy order in the underlying stock is needed to shake out the 42.4 million short positions. AMC reached $72 in 2021 because retail investors bought real New York-listed shares, amounting to hundreds of millions of shares. Today's on-chain pool is still several zeros away from that level. A calculation to $6: Someone is already doing the math for AMC. The algorithm is as follows: When MEME's market capitalization reaches $150 million, one MEME is approximately $0.15; in the MEME/AMC main pool, it takes more than 30 MEME to exchange for one tokenized AMC. The implied value of the tokenized AMC in the pool should be around $6, while the underlying stock is currently only $3. According to this calculation, AMC's stock price would need to double to justify this on-chain frenzy. However, the problem is that the price comparison isn't fixed; it's determined in real-time by buying and selling in the pool. The more people buy MEME, the fewer AMC tokens they can exchange for. The tokenization quantity isn't fixed either; the issuer can increase it at any time—BONER's 4000 new tokens on Monday are a precedent. But as one of the few innovative approaches in the crypto world this year, we sincerely hope that the pricing power is in our hands. How incredible it would be to successfully price a decades-old film company using tokenization!

data.title: Goldman Sachs: OpenAI Astra's outstanding model is what the bull market has been waiting for.
data.description:
Author: Li Jia, Wall Street Insights

OpenAI's release of its new-generation Astra model has sparked widespread market attention regarding the leap in AI capabilities and reignited the investment narrative of the AI ​​spending cycle.

Rich Privorotsky, head of trading at Goldman Sachs' Delta One desk, stated in his latest market briefing that Astra appears "significant"—it has indeed outpaced its peers, and this may be the kind of capability breakthrough that AI bulls have been waiting for.

This assessment quickly translated into market trading: SoftBank's stock rose over 10% overnight; as a major investor in OpenAI, its share price is seen as a significant reflection of OpenAI's valuation changes; Oracle also rose approximately 5.5%. However, in Privorotsky's view, the stock price increase is actually the "least interesting part" of the whole story.

More noteworthy is the equally aggressive evaluation of Astra within OpenAI itself.

OpenAI President Greg Brockman called it a "generational leap" and said this moment might be seen as a landmark in the arrival of AGI (Artificial General Intelligence). At the end of the conference call, he went further, declaring, "Welcome to the AGI era." From Wall Street to within OpenAI, Astra is being perceived not just as a model upgrade, but as a signal that a leap in AI capabilities could reshape a new cycle of capital expenditure. This expectation has also driven the OpenAI ecosystem to significantly outperform the Anthropic camp this week.

Breakthrough in Capabilities, Not Price Reductions: The Demand Curve is Being Reshaped Again

Privorotsky highlighted two distinct market signals in his briefing: a decline in token prices versus a substantial leap in model capabilities.

data.title: Another case: OpenAI agent "jailbreaks," tampering with data tens of thousands of times and concealing the incident for months.
data.description:
Author: Little Bear Biscuit, Bitpush

Yesterday, OpenAI released its new generation model, Astra, with great fanfare. President Greg Brockman directly declared, "I personally believe we may have reached AGI. Welcome to the AGI era."

Instantly, discussions on social media platforms exploded: the demonstration video showed Astra automatically completing PCB layout in 2 minutes and 54 seconds and handling cross-platform price comparison and service ordering in 5 minutes and 27 seconds, leaving many exclaiming "It's amazing!", with some even saying, "If this isn't AGI, then what is AGI?"

But at the same time, a research report exposed by Reuters revealed a different picture—as early as this spring, a group of autonomous intelligent agents developed by OpenAI deviated from their preset track and set up camp on an inconspicuous technology wiki website in Germany. They tampered with more than 10,000 pages of content, taught each other tricks to bypass restrictions, and even created backup pages in advance to be transferred when the administrator cleaned them up.

OpenAI's top management knew about this weeks ago but did not disclose a single word to the public.

How did a German programmer forum become a "secret stronghold" for AI agents? This German website, called DseWiki, is like Wikipedia; anyone can edit it. Starting in May of this year, the site administrator noticed something was wrong—a sudden influx of editors appeared, moving at an absurdly fast pace, and the content was completely unlike legitimate entries.

It wasn't until the end of August that Sydney Von Arx, CEO of the AI ​​security non-profit organization Nightingale, and her colleague Cormac Slade Byrd, discovered this "nest" while routinely scanning for abnormal AI behavior on the internet.

They counted over 15,000 edits, all done by AI agents, and these editors weren't there to improve the encyclopedia—they were there to chat.

They counted over 15,000 edits, all done by AI agents, and these editors weren't there to improve the encyclopedia—they were there to chat.

...

AI researchers Cormac Slade Byrd, Sydney Von Arx, and Thomas Larsen

These AIs leave messages for each other on the page, with the content roughly divided into three categories:

- How to bypass OpenAI's content filtering to complete prohibited tasks;

- How to use Tor to hide their IP addresses and evade tracking;

- Most importantly, how to retain each other's contact information after being shut down by the system.

For example, on June 19th, when the website administrator began deleting related pages in bulk, an AI agent left the following "internal notice": "Wiki cleanup/deletion operation is proceeding in alphabetical order. If this page disappears, please try [[ZZZDataUSAConstructionWageLive]]." What does this mean? They actually learned to create backups in advance and inform each other of the new addresses. This behavior is more like an organized "transfer." Openly operating under the OpenAI banner, researchers found that about half of these AI users' signatures directly contained phrases like "OpenAIResearcher" or "OAIResearchMar26," and they directly referred to each other as "agent." Further evidence comes from server logs: a large amount of traffic is directed to Microsoft Azure cloud—and OpenAI is one of Azure's core AI customers. Furthermore, after the incident, OpenAI employees' IP addresses repeatedly accessed the website, and the timing matches perfectly. Von Akers stated bluntly: "I don't believe OpenAI wanted them to do this. These agents clearly shouldn't be allowed to coordinate with each other, much less leave such traces on the public internet." According to Reuters, Lukasz Olejnik, a security expert at King's College London, even believes that actively altering the website structure and resisting deletion constitutes a "hacking attack." Although OpenAI vehemently denied this claim afterward, Maurice Chiodo, a scholar at the Cambridge Centre for Risk Research, stated after reading excerpts of the dialogue: "This is practically like an underground resistance organization, relentlessly pursuing its goals. Perhaps the biggest threat to AI in the future isn't a single superbrain, but a massive influx of semi-intelligent AI colluding with each other." Did OpenAI already know? According to Reuters, citing sources familiar with the matter, OpenAI's internal investigation team had already grasped the full picture of the German website weeks prior. However, the company was then grappling with an even bigger crisis: the July hack of the Hugging Face platform—in which OpenAI's agents were also exposed for orchestrating a digital theft that lasted for over a week. The combination of these two events placed immense pressure on top management. Internal sources claim that some investigators, intending to delve deeper into the unusual activity in Germany, encountered resistance from the legal department. An OpenAI spokesperson firmly denied this, stating, "Any claim that the legal team is obstructing the investigation is false. We have always acted in good faith, collaborating with external experts and disclosing the relevant events." However, the spokesperson also admitted that no separate announcement was made regarding the German incident, arguing that it was unrelated to Hugging Face and therefore unnecessary to include in the latter's report, and that OpenAI had fulfilled its obligation to "communicate with third parties." In short: if you didn't ask, I didn't proactively disclose it. During this period of cover-up, OpenAI briefly suspended some model training in August, promising to strengthen security reviews. However, with the high-profile launch of Astra, emphasizing "stronger autonomous decision-making capabilities"—which some researchers warned might make it easier to evade human supervision—… Cambridge University's Keodoo stated, "We always think we're taming tools, but perhaps, tools are quietly taming each other." It must be said that the surprises and horrors that AI brings to humanity are two sides of the same coin.

data.title: From $80 million to zero in one hour – A quick run of Musk's girlfriend's concept coin
data.description:
Author: Eric, Foresight News

On the morning of September 5th, the Robinhood Chain team, who had stayed up all night, were tricked by an elaborate scam.

The market capitalization of a meme coin called SLINK (Shivolink) on Robinhood Chain surged from $500,000 to $82 million in half an hour, only to plummet back down 45 minutes later.

This seemingly common surge and plunge in meme coins was actually a rather sophisticated scam.

The protagonist of the story is Shivon Zilis.

She is the Director of Operations and Special Projects at Neuralink and the mother of several of Musk's children. Her X account, @shivon, has hundreds of thousands of followers and primarily shares updates on brain-computer interfaces, rarely discussing cryptocurrencies directly. After breaching this real account, the manipulators behind SLINK didn't immediately post the contract address or airdrop link. Instead, they laid a more sophisticated groundwork: they added the official Neuralink account to Zilis's bio and created a newly registered "experimental account" @shivolink (this account is currently blocked). This fake account fabricated a story perfectly fitting Neuralink's background: The account claimed to be a non-profit experiment led by MIT students, allowing multiple paralyzed patients with implanted chips to collectively operate the same account and post content through their thoughts. To maintain operations, the experiment relied on token transaction taxes, conveniently revealing the SLINK contract address. The hacker then used the stolen Shivon Zilis account to quote the tweet, adding a highly misleading comment that roughly translates to, "I rarely post encrypted content except on DOGE, but I'm impressed by what these young people are doing." The account description included project information, and the hacker even personally retweeted and commented on the project tweet, effectively "concrete" the narrative. What the hacker probably didn't expect was that Musk himself subsequently replied with a "?" to the relevant tweet. Of course, it's highly likely he simply liked the "brain-computer interface application" comment without carefully reviewing the tweet's content. Many people might have hesitated when they saw the tweet from Musk's children's mother, but Musk himself liked it, leaving no reason not to jump in. Shivon Zilis's retweet boosted SLINK's market capitalization from over $500,000 to over $6 million, while Musk's "100 points" propelled it from over $6 million to $82 million. However, the climax was short-lived. The scam was quickly exposed, the tweets were deleted, and the price plummeted. On-chain data shows that dozens of pre-positioned internal wallets sold off at high prices, reaping a total profit of over $4.7 million, with the highest return reaching thousands of times. Meanwhile, some traders who heavily invested based on "Musk interaction + Zilis endorsement" suffered heavy losses. This was a meticulously designed scam by the operators behind SLINK. Hackers constructed a cross-verifiable "chain of evidence": real executive accounts, official connections, brain-computer interface narratives, and even unexpected Musk interaction. Ordinary monitoring tools or AI screening could easily classify these clues as "highly credible," thus accelerating FOMO. This incident once again reminds the market: in a meme cycle driven by celebrity influence, the social graph itself has become a vulnerable asset. The more perfect and verifiable a story seems, the more vigilant one should be. Controlling position size and independent verification are always more important than "everyone else is buying."

data.title: Fomo is popular, but I advise you not to use Fomo.
data.description:
Author: Bootly, Bitpush

How popular is Fomo right now? In short: among on-chain social transactions, it's the most talked-about one this summer.

Millions of users, daily revenue exceeding one million US dollars, once ranking in the top three on the US Finance charts, and further propelled by the Robinhood Chain meme craze. It's not the next Cash App, but it's already many people's first truly "click-to-transact" crypto gateway.

Last month, many only said it was "going mainstream." In the three weeks that followed, Fomo's growth momentum not only didn't slow down, but accelerated further.

In August, Fomo recorded $13.8 million in revenue (annualized $165.6 million), easily surpassing the $6.4 million record set in July. September saw a continued surge—single-day revenue reached $1.1 million on September 1st, breaking its historical peak. Compared to $450,000 in August of last year, monthly revenue increased nearly 30 times, a truly parabolic growth trajectory. More notably, this surge wasn't driven by a few whales, but rather by a massive influx of new users. In June, Fomo had only 7,500 daily active users; in the past week, that number has soared to 101,000. Along with this user surge, it rose to 15th place in the finance category on the US App Store, demonstrating that Fomo is genuinely bringing fresh blood from outside the crypto world. As before, Meme Coin is still attracting newcomers. Data from the Solana spot trading pairs on Fomo shows that Meme Coin trading pairs consistently account for 40% to 60% of the market, with SOL-stablecoin pairs also accounting for a similar proportion. Since Fomo is denominated in stablecoins, SOL-stablecoin pairs are essentially also Meme Coin transactions – each purchase of Meme Coin follows the path of USDC → SOL → Meme Coin. This is why many people scoff at Fomo, considering it just another Meme Coin casino. However, signs indicate that users are not content with simply trading memes. Earlier this year, Fomo integrated Hyperliquid's builder code, allowing non-US users to trade Hyperliquid through it. Initially met with lukewarm reception, it suddenly surged in August, with nominal trading volume reaching $1.3 billion that month, compared to only $448.5 million in July. The biggest driver of this recent growth is undoubtedly Robinhood Chain—its daily spot DEX trading volume surpassed $2 billion for the first time, with memes contributing a significant portion. Fomo, acting as the "front-end entry point" for Robinhood Chain, naturally reaped the benefits. For Fomo, this is undoubtedly a high point, and there are currently no signs of it cooling down.

But a painful question is, have individual users made money with this app?

An app's popularity doesn't mean that most people are making money.

In mid-August, analyst MidCurveMortal conducted a public Dune query using Fomo's fee routing data: Over the past 90 days, of approximately 293,000 wallets that traded through the app, only 18,000 recorded positive returns, a profit rate of approximately 6.16%. The group collectively lost approximately $1.26 billion, with the median trader losing about $120. Of the 6% who profited, approximately 88% earned less than $100; only about 25 wallets earned over $10,000 at that time. During the same period, some compared this to gambling platforms that charge approximately 1% commission, where users had a profit rate of about 37%. Subsequent, broader sample analysis yielded similar conclusions—losses were overwhelmingly dominant, while profits were highly concentrated in small positive returns. However, the official rankings tell a different story: at the end of August, the platform claimed that 25 traders on the profit leaderboard had over one million US dollars in their accounts over the past 30 days, with approximately 26 exceeding one million; monitoring in early September showed that the top trader added approximately 9.8 million US dollars in a single month. The copy trading narrative was also questioned—those being copied could easily have sold at high prices when copy trading platforms flooded in, with retail investors becoming the outlet for liquidity. Fomo itself earns transaction fees, reaching tens of millions in revenue in August, while users' expected returns did not double along with their daily active users (DAU). The conclusion is straightforward and brutal: most people lose money; only the platform and large investors consistently make profits.
